name: Small Business Checklist
description: An ongoing checklist for running and managing an established small business.

items.text: Review and update standard operating procedures for key tasks.
Check inventory or supply levels and reorder as needed.
Confirm equipment and tools are maintained and working.
Renew software subscriptions and review what you actually use.
Back up business data and verify the backup is recoverable.
Clear outstanding admin tasks and tidy your filing system.
Review supplier performance and renegotiate terms where possible.
Reconcile bank accounts against your bookkeeping records.
Send invoices promptly and chase overdue payments.
Pay bills and suppliers on time to protect relationships.
Review cash flow and forecast the next few months.
Set aside funds for tax obligations as you earn.
items.note: Tax rules and rates vary by country and state — confirm with your authority.

items.text: Compare actual income and expenses against your budget.
Review pricing and margins to make sure you stay profitable.
Confirm licenses and permits are current and renewed on time.
items.note: Requirements vary by jurisdiction — check your official government authority.

items.text: Review business insurance coverage against your current risks.
Keep contracts and key agreements organized and up to date.
File required tax and regulatory returns by their deadlines.
Check that data and privacy practices meet applicable rules.
Document important records and store them securely.
Review which marketing channels bring you the best customers.
Publish fresh content or offers to stay visible to your audience.
Update your website and listings with current information.
Request and respond to customer reviews.
Follow up with past customers to encourage repeat business.
Track leads and conversion to see what's working.
Plan promotions around upcoming busy or slow periods.
Respond to customer enquiries and complaints promptly.
Collect feedback and look for recurring issues to fix.
Review service or delivery times and quality.
Update FAQs and self-service resources for common questions.
Reward or recognize loyal customers.
Check in with team members and address any concerns.
Confirm payroll and any benefits are processed correctly.
items.note: Employment obligations vary by jurisdiction — verify locally.

items.text: Schedule training to close skill gaps.
Review staffing levels against your workload.
Set goals for the coming quarter and track progress.
Identify one improvement to test and grow the business.

faq.q: How often should I work through this checklist?
faq.a: Treat most items as a monthly review, with finance and compliance tasks revisited monthly or quarterly. Some items, like backups and customer follow-up, are best done weekly. Adjust the cadence to your workload.

faq.q: I'm a solo owner — is this still useful?
faq.a: Yes. Solo owners benefit most from a routine because there's no one else to catch gaps. Skip team items if they don't apply and focus on operations, finance and marketing.

faq.q: How do I keep my finances healthy as a small business?
faq.a: Reconcile accounts regularly, separate business and personal money, watch cash flow closely, and set aside funds for taxes. The finance section here turns those habits into a repeatable routine.

faq.q: Does this cover legal and tax requirements?
faq.a: It includes general reminders such as renewing licenses and filing on time. Specific legal and tax obligations vary by country and state, so confirm details with your official government authority or a qualified professional.

faq.q: Can I download this as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the checklist for your wall or download the PDF to reuse each month and share with your team or accountant.
